newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ gas mkt competition sought with new regulations.
newsitem.headline: NZ gas mkt competition sought with new regulations.

text.p: Information disclosure regulations designed to encourage competition in the New Zealand gas industry will come into force on August 7, Energy Minister Max Bradford said on Tuesday.
"I expect to see more competition between gas retailers, with benefits for consumers," Bradford said in a statement.
"Perhaps more important, however, is the prospect of new wholesalers entering the market."
Bradford said the keys to wholesale gas competition were the availability of gas supplies and access to pipelines.
"Information disclosure is designed to help open up access to pipelines and reinforce the industry's own efforts to implement a pipeline access code," he said.

The Gas (Information Disclosure) Regulations focus on natural monopoly pipeline businesses. As for electricity, the information disclosure regulations aim to separate the natural monopoly elements of distribution from the potentially competitive wholesale and retail sectors of the gas industry.

"The aim is to create an environment where competition for gas supply can develop. It is a key element of the light-handed regulatory framework for both the electricity and gas sectors," Bradford said.
Under the new regulations, gas companies will be required to disclose:
* separate financial statements for transmission, wholesale, distribution and retail businesses;
* financial, efficiency and reliability performance measures;
* pipeline capacity information and line charges.
